sources.title: Night Watch in One Brain Hemisphere during Sleep Associated with the First-Night Effect in Humans
sources.why_it_matters: Proved in 35 human sleepers via simultaneous MEG, structural MRI, and polysomnography that the left default-mode network stays in shallow slow-wave 'night-watch' vigilance on Night 1 and reacts faster to deviant sounds.

sources.title: THE FIRST NIGHT EFFECT: AN EEG STUDYOF SLEEP
sources.why_it_matters: Classic behavioral and EEG discovery of the human First-Night Effect showing delayed sleep onset, fragmented stages, and heightened nocturnal vigilance in unfamiliar bedrooms.

sources.title: Infraslow noradrenergic locus coeruleus activity fluctuations are gatekeepers of the NREM–REM sleep cycle
sources.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that infraslow noradrenergic locus coeruleus pulses gate micro-arousals and sensory vigilance windows during NREM sleep.

sources.title: Research progress on the first‐night effect in polysomnography studies
sources.why_it_matters: Reviewed boundary conditions and inter-individual variability of first-night polysomnography adaptation across clinical vs home environments.

sources.title: Surveillance During REM Sleep for the First-Night Effect
sources.why_it_matters: Extended first-night neural surveillance findings into REM sleep theta oscillations and brain-wide vigilance gating.

sources.title: Behavioral, neurophysiological and evolutionary perspectives on unihemispheric sleep
sources.why_it_matters: Comparative neuroscience benchmark of unihemispheric slow-wave night-watch sleep across cetaceans and migratory birds.
